name: pointer-highlight

frames.best_why: All three rectangles are fully drawn with their cursor arrows parked at the corners and no stray pointer.

tagline: Thin boxes draw around text and finish with a small cursor arrow.
summary: Wraps a line of text in a thin rectangle that draws itself when it scrolls into view, with a little click cursor landing at the bottom-right corner in a colour you choose.
appearance: Three short lines of white text on black, each inside a thin rectangular outline with sharp corners. A small arrow cursor sits just outside each box's bottom-right corner, two blue and one green.
behaviour: When the text scrolls into view the border grows out from the corner while a cursor fades in and slides to the bottom-right, then everything holds still.
demo_content: Lines 'Ship faster than ever', 'Build beautiful interfaces with zero friction' and 'Open source · MIT license'.
search_phrases: cursor arrow pointing at a block
landing page line with a pointer
marketing text with a box around it
use_when: A short line in a hero should feel pointed at, as if someone circled it in a design review.
avoid_when: It draws once and stays: there is no hover response despite the cursor glyph, so it cannot stay interactive.
customise: Wrap the content and recolour the box and arrow with rectangleClassName and pointerClassName; draw timing and cursor placement are in the source.
weight_why: Two short draw animations per wrapped block, fired once when it enters view.

a11y.note: The border and cursor are purely decorative, and the draw animation ignores reduced-motion.

issues: While the border is drawing, the cursor arrow sits on top of the words and reads as an overlap.
polish_why: Crisp, well-timed box with a charming cursor; the arrow overlaps the text while drawing.
title: Pointer Highlight
